title.value: Revive old MacBook Airs as headless Mac mini extensions

introduction.value: A user had Hermes Agent help turn two old MacBook Air laptops into headless extensions of a Mac mini and asked it for directive text for each agent.

method.value: The user had Hermes Agent help repurpose two shelf-bound 2020 Intel MacBook Airs, each with 8GB RAM and 256GB storage, into headless companions for a Mac mini. Hermes guided cleanup of unused storage and memory, then, with the user helping, walked through adding Tailscale and CLI tools; in follow-up comments, the user said Hermes also helped change settings so the laptops stayed awake with the lids closed.

outcome.value: The setup worked within the machines’ storage and memory limits, and let the user shut down a Hetzner VPS, saving about $15 a month. It took a few hours total, or roughly an hour per device, rather than being instant.

notes.value: The user says the whole project used under $0.50 of DeepSeek API spend.

source_text.body:
Revive old MacBook Airs as headless Mac mini extensions
A user had Hermes Agent help turn two old MacBook Air laptops into headless extensions of a Mac mini and asked it for directive text for each agent.
Done with
HA
Hermes Agent
What they did
The user had Hermes Agent help repurpose two shelf-bound 2020 Intel MacBook Airs, each with 8GB RAM and 256GB storage, into headless companions for a Mac mini. Hermes guided cleanup of unused storage and memory, then, with the user helping, walked through adding Tailscale and CLI tools; in follow-up comments, the user said Hermes also helped change settings so the laptops stayed awake with the lids closed.
How it went
The setup worked within the machines’ storage and memory limits, and let the user shut down a Hetzner VPS, saving about $15 a month. It took a few hours total, or roughly an hour per device, rather than being instant.
Worth knowing
The user says the whole project used under $0.50 of DeepSeek API spend.
Try it yourself
with
Hermes Agent
Copy prompt
I want to turn my old [laptop model] into a headless extension of my [main computer, e.g. Mac mini]. Walk me through the setup step by step, covering remote access, auto-login, sleep settings, and how the machines share work, and tell me what to run on each one. Then write a short directive text for the agent on each machine describing its role: [role of main machine], [role of laptop 1], [role of laptop 2]. Pause and show me any command that changes system settings or erases data before running it. You are done when I can reach each laptop remotely and each agent has its directive.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/hermesagent/comments/1usj9yh/what_have_you_done_with_hermes_agent_this_week
